data.title: ICE Canada Morning Comment: ICE Canola Futures Softer
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures were posting small losses Friday morning as values continued to chop around in narrow, rangebound trade.

The January contract was down $2.50 at C$774.50 per tonne in early activity.

Overnight losses in Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil accounted for some spillover selling pressure.

Canada exported 141,000 tonnes of canola during the week ended Nov. 15, which was roughly half of what moved the previous week, reported the Canadian Grain Commission.

However, marketing-year-to-date exports of 2.66 million tonnes remain well ahead of the 1.83 million tonnes exported by the same point in 2025-26.

Updated supply/demand estimates from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada included only minor adjustments to the canola balance sheet, with projected 2026-27 ending stocks lowered to 1.87 million tonnes from 1.97 million in October.

Projected exports for the year were left unchanged at 7.7 million tonnes, while domestic usage was raised by 100,000 tonnes to 14.5 million.

About 14,300 canola contracts had traded as of 8:46 a.m. ET.

data.title: Vallourec Shares Plunge on Disappointing Guidance, U.S. Concerns
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Vallourec shares fell sharply Friday after guidance for the final quarter of the year disappointed investors and the company flagged an operational issue in the U.S.

Shares were 11% lower in afternoon European trade.

The French manufacturer of tubes and pipes to the oil and gas, auto and other industrial markets said that the temporary operational issue relates to a subcontractor and contributed to lower-than-expected sequential improvement in its U.S. business in the third quarter.

At the same time, while crude exports and drilling activity have picked up in the Middle East, a recent deterioration in the maritime security situation in the region has created logistical disruptions and higher costs that led to delays in deliveries and invoicing.

"With tube inventories in the region largely depleted, the need to prioritize tube shipments to maintain drilling operations and ensure adequate stocks is becoming critical," Chief Executive Officer Philippe Guillemot said in a statement.

The renewed escalation in the Middle East has clouded visibility and heightened near-term shipment risks, while the temporary operational issue in the U.S. business is also expected to constrain an improvement in the business that was expected in the fourth quarter, Guillemot added.

Vallourec expects group fourth-quarter earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization of between $170 million and $210 million.

Analysts at Jefferies said in a note to clients that Friday's share price reaction appears largely due to the uncertainty around the U.S. operational issue. Nevertheless, the bank said the extent of the price fall seems overdone, given that many investors acknowledged that consensus appeared too high amid the continued Middle East logistics risk.

"Whilst we had been cautious on the 4Q guide, which is -25% versus consensus, the extent of today's reaction surprises us."

data.title: Italy seeks security safeguards in Finnish bid for rocket maker Avio, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Italy wants Avio to retain a domestic presence in any deal
  • Rome sees Leonardo as key partner post-deal
  • Meloni government wary of strategic asset sales

By Angelo Amante, Giuseppe Fonte and Elvira Pollina

Italy's government wants to ensure a €2 billion ($2.2 billion) bid by Finland's Iceye for rocket maker Avio preserves the company's domestic presence and favours keeping state-controlled defence group Leonardo as a key shareholder, three people with direct knowledge of the matter said.

The likely conditions are aimed at protecting national security and preserving sovereign oversight over Avio, which makes propulsion systems for space rockets, the people said.

Finnish satellite operator Iceye made a cash offer on Tuesday for Milan-listed Avio, with the aim of creating an integrated European space and defence group that could reduce reliance on external providers such as Elon Musk's Starshield.

While Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's right-wing government is not opposed in principle to foreign investment, it would seek to maintain control over technologies linked to national security, the three people said.

Meloni's office declined to comment.

Rome's concerns focus particularly on Avio's expertise in solid-fuel rocket motors, the people said, a capability considered strategically sensitive as Europe aims to strengthen its defence industrial base and reduce dependence on non-European suppliers.

The people said Italy wants any deal to ensure that Avio remains partly Italian and that national sovereignty over solid-rocket motors is preserved. Details of any conditions remain unclear as authorities have not yet begun formal scrutiny of the bid.

They added that the government sees Leonardo , which has an 18% stake in Avio, as the natural partner to preserve Italian influence over the company.

Iceye and Leonardo declined to comment on any conditions that may be tied to the deal.

GOLDEN POWER OVER SOME ASSETS

Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani welcomed the bid, but Defence Minister Guido Crosetto urged caution over any stake sale, signalling the government's reluctance to fully hand over control of the company to a foreign buyer.

Since taking office in 2022, Meloni's government has repeatedly used powers designed to protect assets in sectors including defence, aerospace, telecommunications and energy.

Under Italy's so-called golden power rules, Rome can impose conditions on acquisitions in these sectors or, in extreme cases, block them. A fourth person familiar with the matter said the government has not been formally notified of the Avio transaction.

A spokesperson for Iceye said the company had initiated "the relevant regulatory process in Italy" and was engaging with the competent authorities.

data.description:
Sweetgreen, Inc. () today announced that the company is scheduled to present at the Morgan Stanley Global Consumer & Retail Conference on December 2, 2026. The company will participate in a fireside chat at the conference that will begin at 11:45 am ET.

A live webcast and replay of the fireside chat will be available at investor.sweetgreen.com on the Events + Presentations page.

About Sweetgreen: Sweetgreen () believes good taste starts long before the first bite. Since 2007, the brand has been on a mission to create healthy communities by connecting people to real food. Its longstanding relationships with farmers bring seasonal ingredients to its kitchens, where teams cook from scratch every day. The result is a fresh, flavorful approach to fast casual that makes eating well something to look forward to. Today, sweetgreen offers its farm-sourced, chef-crafted menus at 290 locations across the country.

Marriott Vacations Worldwide (“MVW”) () today announced the appointment of Aaron Broholm as Vice President, Investor Relations. Broholm will report to Jason Marino, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120931255/en/

Aaron Broholm, Vice President, Investor Relations, Marriott Vacations Worldwide

In this role, Broholm will lead the company’s investor relations strategy and engagement with shareholders, analysts and the broader investment community. He will work closely with the company’s executive leadership team to communicate MVW’s financial performance, strategic priorities and long-term growth objectives.

"Aaron has built his career helping investors understand and believe in a company's vision, with a proven ability to navigate some of the most complex shareholder environments," said Marino. "His expertise and credibility with the investment community will be invaluable in earning the market's long-term confidence, and we're glad to have him on board as we continue to execute our growth strategy."

Broholm brings more than 20 years of experience across investor relations, corporate finance, tax and public company communications. Most recently, he served as Head of Investor Relations for The Wendy’s Company, where he led investor communications and engagement for the global restaurant brand. Prior to Wendy’s, he spent 14 years with The J.M. Smucker Company, including nearly a decade as Vice President of Investor Relations. In that role, he oversaw corporate positioning, earnings communications, shareholder and analyst engagement, investor conferences and market intelligence.

“Marriott Vacations Worldwide has a compelling story to tell, and I look forward to working alongside the leadership team to strengthen engagement with the investment community and reinforce the long-term value of the business,” said Broholm. “I’m honored to help the company continue to build on its momentum.”

About Marriott Vacations Worldwide Corporation

Marriott Vacations Worldwide Corporation is a leading global vacation company that offers vacation ownership, exchange, rental and resort and property management, along with related businesses, products, and services. The Company has approximately 120 vacation ownership resorts and approximately 650,000 owner families in a diverse portfolio that includes some of the most iconic vacation ownership brands. The Company also operates an exchange network and membership programs comprised of more than 3,200 affiliated resorts in over 90 countries and territories, and provides management services to other resorts and lodging properties. As a leader and innovator in the vacation industry, the Company upholds the highest standards of excellence in serving its customers, investors and associates while maintaining exclusive, long-term relationships with Marriott International, Inc. and an affiliate of Hyatt Hotels Corporation for the development, sales and marketing of vacation ownership products and services. data.title: 2026 Sustainability Brief Highlights Emissions Reporting, Fleet Efficiency and Investments in People as Werner® Marks 70 Years of Service
data.description:
Werner Enterprises, Inc. (), a premier transportation and logistics provider, today released its sixth annual sustainability report, the 2026 Sustainability Brief. The brief connects the company’s sustainability efforts with the operational priorities that matter to customers: reliable service, efficient freight movement and better visibility into supply chain emissions.

“For 70 years, Werner has helped keep America moving by investing in our people, our equipment and the service we deliver,” said Werner’s Chairman and CEO, Derek Leathers. “We are almost halfway to our goal of a 55% reduction in CO₂ emissions by 2035 against our 2020 baseline. Our sixth annual sustainability report highlights the practical investments in fleet efficiency, technology and emissions reporting that support our continued progress and help our customers meet their sustainability goals.”

Key highlights from the 2026 Sustainability Brief include:

  • Fleet Decarbonization & Equipment Innovation: Advanced a practical, multi-pathway decarbonization strategy by evaluating and piloting diverse low- and zero-emission technologies and fuels.

  • Emissions Reduction & Expanded Reporting: Achieved a 27% reduction in CO2 emissions relative to its 2020 baseline. Expanded transparency by refining Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG accounting controls and disclosing Scope 3 supply chain emissions for the first time.

  • Waste Reduction & Environmental Stewardship: Utilized the Waste and Energy Scorecard to track resource efficiency, conserving more than 619,000 gallons of oil through tire retreading, recycling more than 850,000 pounds of metal and returning nearly 14,000 battery cores to production loops.

  • Strengthened Governance & Global Frameworks: Aligned reporting with SASB standards, UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and CDP climate disclosures. Established a formal Greenhouse Gas Inventory Management Plan (IMP) to prepare for future limited assurance reporting and mandatory compliance requirements.

The 2026 Sustainability Brief is available for download here.

About Werner Enterprises

Werner Enterprises, Inc. ("Werner") delivers superior truckload transportation and logistics services to customers across the United States, Mexico and Canada. With Werner® 2025 revenues of nearly $3.0 billion, a modern truck and trailer fleet, more than 14,800 talented associates and our innovative Werner EDGE® technology, we are an essential solutions provider for customers who value the integrity of their supply chain and require safe and exceptional on-time service. In January 2026, Werner acquired FirstEnterprises, Inc. ("FirstFleet"), which generated more than $600 million in unaudited 2025 revenues. Werner provides Dedicated and One-Way Truckload services as well as Logistics services that include truckload brokerage, freight management, intermodal and final mile. Werner embraces inclusion as a core value and manages key risks and opportunities through a balanced sustainability strategy.

data.title: After Brexit, Britain's Government Floats 'Breturn' — WSJ
data.description:
By Max Colchester in London and Laurence Norman in Berlin

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham is resurrecting the ghost of Brexit.

Six years after the U.K.'s acrimonious and chaotic break with the European Union, Burnham wants the country to consider a major U-turn and rejoin the trade bloc to bolster the British economy.

On Friday, the Labour Party leader traveled to Brussels to unveil a set of agreements aimed at marking a "reset" in U.K.-EU relations, including scrapping most border checks on food and agricultural products and reintroducing a student-exchange program.

Burnham's visit was aimed at kicking off a wider debate about an issue that has divided British society and dogged politicians for decades: To what extent should the U.K. integrate with its biggest trade partner?

"In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together," Burnham said Friday.

But even those limited deals proved fraught and fell short of expectations, suggesting any further talks aimed at a deeper relationship between both sides will be long and arduous.

While Burnham cast the "reset" deals as done, European negotiators said none of the agreements will be fully implemented unless European students could get lower tuition rates at U.K. universities. Both sides agreed to continue to negotiate student fees over the next six months.

The issue of Europe has finally cooled in British politics after years of heated debate that cut across party and class lines and often divided families. In a 2016 referendum, 52% of the British public voted to leave the EU, leading to a formal departure from the bloc four years later. Now, driven by public disappointment over how Brexit has played out, the government is wondering whether it should re-enter, raising the prospect that Brexit, followed by "Bregret", will lead eventually to "Breturn."

Raising trade barriers has slowed trade growth between both sides, hurting the British economy alongside the pandemic and the war in Ukraine that spiked energy prices. It also backfired spectacularly in immigration, with Britain closing access to European workers but allowing in millions more from the rest of the world.

An average of polls shows that 62% of Brits would like to rejoin the EU, compared with 38% who want to stay out. "The Brexit we were given has not worked," Burnham said in a speech this week. "We have lost more than we have gained." Research by Goldman Sachs suggests that rejoining the EU's single market would bolster the U.K. economy by between 2% and 5%.

Rejoining, though, would be a long and possibly costly process. The prospect will reopen a painful debate, including among working-class voters in Burnham's own Labour Party. There is no guarantee that Britain would get the same advantages it had the first time around, including getting to keep its own currency or a discount on membership fees it previously enjoyed. Without those advantages, polls show wavering public support for rejoining.

"There isn't a button you can press to go back to 2016," said Anand Menon, who runs the think tank U.K. in a Changing Europe, noting that Breturn could become politically all-consuming, creating uncertainty that could weigh on the economy in the short term and distract the government from sorting out pressing domestic issues.

"Thinking it's a bad idea you left is not the same as thinking you should join," he added.

Already, the siren call of another argument over Europe has reinvigorated the old Brexit guard. A campaign called "Stay Out" is pumping out content on social media. Burnham "will impale himself and his party on this point, and he needs to move off it because he won't win," said Boris Johnson, a former U.K. prime minister and Brexit cheerleader.

David Cameron, the former prime minister who pledged to end the debate over Europe once and for all by calling the referendum, said the government should focus on other problems plaguing Britain's economy, including ever-higher taxes, spending and debt, a lack of housing and the need to shore up the country's diminished armed forces.

A YouGov survey put rejoining the EU at No. 9 on a list of voter priorities, well behind the economy, immigration and healthcare.

Burnham, who has said he wants Britain to rejoin in his lifetime, said Friday he wants to use the next year for informal discussions with top EU officials over the options available for a new longer-term relationship. It isn't yet clear what those options are, or how Brits would choose — either through another referendum or as part of the next general election, which could be as late as 2029.

Burnham said Friday that it will be for British voters to decide. He acknowledged that Friday's agreements probably hit the limit of increased cooperation the two sides can achieve before the next election.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, the EU's top official, said she was receptive to brainstorming with the U.K. on the future relationship and hit an optimistic note on Friday.

"We have already achieved a great deal together and as partners, allies and friends, we have every reason to be ambitious about what comes next," she said during a press conference.

Nonetheless, Europe will want to know what exactly Britain is seeking before it enters any serious negotiations. The last thing the trade club needs is Britain yo-yoing in and out depending on the political whim of the day.

"It's not priority No. 1 for the EU and they will want to be convinced that whatever Britain comes up with in terms of proposing a new relationship, it's something that will last," said Rosa Balfour, director of Carnegie Europe.

Most economists agree Brexit has been an economic mistake. But they also point out Britain hasn't taken advantage of it by making its economy much more competitive through steps like deregulation.

In fact, the quest to rejoin may be starting just as Brexit does bear some fruit. The U.K.'s economy has performed better than expected in recent quarters, in part due to what economists say is faster AI adoption. Some fear that signing up to the EU's more stringent AI regulation could snuff out a growth avenue for the country.

On some levels, Britain still needs Europe and vice versa. The war in Ukraine, a flood of cheap Chinese exports and strains with Washington are forcing European capitals to close ranks. Burnham's argument is that Britain will also have to link arms with Europe to contend with this new fractured world order. "We can't ignore this reality, nor the fact that we have a club of democracies on our doorstep which shares so many of our values and our interests," he said recently.

The U.K. isn't alone in debating the EU. Icelanders recently voted narrowly to reject membership negotiations with the bloc. The EU and Switzerland have spent more than a decade renegotiating their relationship, and Swiss voters will hold a referendum on the result. Half a dozen Balkan countries, Ukraine and Moldova have spent years trying to enter.

There is a large menu of options, each with trade-offs. The U.K. could seek to enter a customs union — free movement for goods and a common external tariff for imports. That would ease two-way trade and allow Britain to keep regulatory control over services. But there would still be some checks on the flow of British goods to the EU's single market.

A bolder step would be to seek access to the single market, like Norway, but it would have to pay into some EU programs and allow workers to move freely as well as accept EU rules without any say in how they are made. The third option — full EU membership — would come with higher EU payments and freedom of movement but it would allow Britain to have a vote on the trade bloc's rules.

Meanwhile, new trade divergences are being erected between the EU and the U.K. The bloc's "Made in Europe" plan to force Chinese automakers to produce cars in the EU would also place tariffs on electric-vehicle exports from Britain.

Labour's previous prime minister, Keir Starmer, who brought Labour back into power in 2024, tried to stymie a broader debate over Brexit by barring his party from considering re-entering the EU's customs union, single market or full membership, at least until the next election.

At a minimum, Burnham looks likely to erase those red lines when he fights the next election.

data.title: US Treasury presses Singapore and Malaysia on Iran sanctions compliance
data.description:
Key points:
  • Washington warns of more enforcement actions in Asia to end conflict in Middle East
  • US aims to cripple Iran's economy with sanctions on oil trade and front companies
  • Officials raised Tehran-Kuala Lumpur flights with Malaysian government

By Gregor Stuart Hunter

US Treasury Department officials met with government authorities in Singapore and Malaysia this week, including regulators and national security bodies, to warn of potential risks they could face if they do not comply with US sanctions on Iran.

Washington is urging the countries, as well as law firms and banks operating there, to stay alert for Iranian front companies, as it steps up efforts to enforce sanctions in Asia and bring about a speedy end to the conflict in the Middle East.

The US is urging additional scrutiny on "high-risk" sectors such as maritime transport, aviation services and procurement networks, "to make sure they're not fronting for Iran," said a Treasury Department official.

"We want it to be understood too, that we're going to target these lifelines, and it's not going to be a negotiation when we find a lifeline that needs to be targeted," the official said.

Since the US and Israel commenced strikes on Iran in February, the US has intensified actions to throttle Tehran's business interests overseas.

In August, President Donald Trump's administration launched Operation Economic Outcast, resulting in a barrage of sanctions against targets spanning Canadian digital currency platforms to a major Russian banking group.

OIL ON WATER

For years, tankers have regularly made stops in the waters around Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia to make ship-to-ship transfers of Iranian oil that help obscure its origin.

Last year, Malaysian authorities said they would more tightly enforce rules around these transfers and in February seized two tankers and their cargoes.

Since April, the US Navy has imposed a blockade on shipping reaching Iran through the Strait of Hormuz, and this month has cracked down on movement over Iran's land borders and through the Caspian Sea.

In July, the Treasury Department sanctioned dozens of individuals, vessels and companies based in Singapore, Hong Kong, the UAE, the Marshall Islands and St Kitts and Nevis linked to Iranian oil magnate Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

These efforts were starting to disrupt Iran's source of revenue, the US official said, citing data showing that the country is currently undergoing the worst GDP contraction in four decades and the highest rate of inflation since World War II.

IRANIAN AIRLINES

However, the official said there was still work to be done.

"There's an Iranian airline that flies to Malaysia, or has, recently, so we raised this," the US official said, without naming the carrier.

Using public flight records, Reuters identified a regularly scheduled flight between Tehran and Kuala Lumpur operated by Iran Airtour, which flew as recently as November 14. A scheduled flight on November 17 did not depart, the records also show.

Iran Airtour did not respond to an emailed request for comment sent outside of business hours on Friday.

Most Iranian airlines largely stopped flying to Malaysia in 2022 due to US sanctions on refuelling Iranian planes. However, Iran Airtour, a privately owned airline, resumed flights to Malaysia in November 2025, according to Iranian media.

On September 8, the US imposed sanctions on dozens of companies in the UAE, Britain, Malaysia, Turkey and Kazakhstan it said were supporting Iran's aviation sector to move weapons, personnel and illicit cargo.

The following day, Iran Air officials met with Malaysia's ambassador to Iran to discuss resuming direct flights between Iran and Kuala Lumpur.

'DOING OUR PART'

Both Malaysia and Singapore implement UN Security Council sanctions on Iran.

Singapore's government said in a statement it "is firmly committed to doing our part" and "preventing bad actors from abusing our corporate vehicles," citing its efforts to strengthen vigilance in the maritime and financial industries this year.

The Malaysian government did not respond to requests for comment.

data.title: Gold, Silver Drop to Lowest Levels in Over a Year — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Megan Cheah and Farhan Rafid

Gold and silver prices fell to their lowest levels in over a year on Friday as a broader selloff across commodities and expectations of higher interest rates globally pressured precious metals.

Expectations for tighter monetary policy appear to have overshadowed the typical demand for gold as a safe haven for risk-averse investors. The precious metals weakened despite heavy losses across Asian stock markets.

December gold futures fell 3.4% to $3,561.70 a troy ounce, while spot silver declined around 2.1% to $41.84 an ounce.

The decline in precious metals is part of a broader selloff across commodities, with investors cutting exposure, unwinding crowded positions and taking profits ahead of year-end, according to Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank.

Hansen said in a note Friday that precious metals had suffered the largest losses, with silver falling 14% and gold nearly 8% this week. Rising borrowing costs, a stronger U.S. dollar and concerns about artificial-intelligence investment have added to selling pressure, while losses in other assets have increased demand for cash.

Gold's failure to attract safe-haven demand during the equity-market selloff suggests investors are selling liquid assets to cover losses and reduce risk, Hansen said. However, holdings in gold exchange-traded funds have remained broadly unchanged over the past month despite the decline in prices, indicating longer-term investors have largely maintained their exposure.

The gold-to-silver ratio rose as high as 85.65 Friday, about 25% above its average over nearly three decades. The ratio measures how many ounces of silver are needed to buy an ounce of gold, with a higher reading indicating silver is relatively cheaper.

Julius Baer analyst Carsten Menke said silver's decline below $45 an ounce, alongside a gold-to-silver ratio above 85, could present a buying opportunity. However, the bank is waiting for signs that prices have bottomed before turning more positive, as further declines remain possible. Julius Baer maintains a neutral view on silver and a constructive outlook for gold.

Copper also declined, with December futures falling 2.4% to $5.4965 a pound. The industrial metal is on track to lose around 9% this week, reaching an eight-month low amid concerns about global growth, Chinese demand and the outlook for artificial-intelligence infrastructure investment, according to Saxo Bank.

Julius Baer upgraded its outlook for copper to constructive following the recent correction, saying the metal remains at risk of a structural supply deficit as demand from electric vehicles, clean energy and battery storage increases. Copper prices have fallen more than 15% from their highs this year, but the bank expects electrification-related technologies to account for around 30% of demand by 2035, compared with 25% in 2025. Menke said mining investments are increasing but might come too late to prevent a shortage.

Japan's consumer inflation data for October, released Friday, showed prices were accelerating past the Bank of Japan's target. That reinforced expectations for tighter policy as policymakers grew increasingly worried about the risk of higher prices due to increased energy costs, persistent yen weakness and rising semiconductor prices amid the artificial-intelligence boom.

"A rate hike at the next meeting in December looks highly likely, and the central bank will likely discuss an additional increase in March 2027, when inflation is expected to accelerate into the 3% range," said Takeshi Minami, an economist at Norinchukin Research Institute.

Minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve's October meeting, released Wednesday, also showed that nearly all policymakers expected higher interest rates would be needed to lower inflation.

The minutes "showed strong alignment from Fed officials on the need for additional rate hikes," said MUFG analysts. Markets recently priced in a 93% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month.

Many also expect the European Central Bank to raise rates in December after staying on hold last month, as it is under pressure to address the inflationary backdrop given persistently high energy prices.

A higher interest-rate environment typically diminishes the allure of nonyielding assets such as gold and silver. The hawkish Fed view also likely lifted the dollar, which makes gold and silver--both dollar-denominated commodities--more expensive for investors holding other currencies.

Upcoming U.S. economic data could shape expectations for the size of a December interest-rate move by the Fed, said Critical Metals' Tony Sage in a note. This includes the second estimate for the country's third-quarter gross domestic product growth due next week.

"Firm readings could lift yields further and extend gold's losses, while softer prints may offer some relief," he added.

data.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Flash PMI Data to Provide Gauge on Economic Growth
data.description:
By Dow Jones Newswires staff

Below are the most important global events likely to affect FX and bond markets in the week starting Nov. 23.

November's flash purchasing managers' surveys for the U.S., eurozone and U.K. will be among the key events. The surveys are an important measure of economic activity and could signal whether there is scope for the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of England to raise interest rates further.

In the U.S, markets will also be closely monitoring Personal Consumption Expenditures price data, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure.

In the Asia-Pacific region, South Korea's interest-rate decision will lead the week, with most analysts expecting a quarter-point increase as strong chip exports fuel growth and inflation remains above target. Inflation data from Australia and Tokyo, along with remarks from a Bank of Japan policy board member, could shape expectations for rate increases in both countries.

China will report October industrial profits as investors watch for Beijing's response to tighter U.S. chip export restrictions.

U.S.

U.S. economic activity and inflation will help investors gauge the path of interest rates in a week shortened by a major holiday.

November's flash manufacturing and services PMI numbers are on tap Monday, as well as a speech by New York Federal Reserve President John Williams at the University of Mount Saint Vincent.

September housing indicators are likely to draw attention Tuesday, as elevated mortgage rates weigh on the sector.

The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index is also scheduled for Tuesday, as consumption continues to be a source of strength for the U.S. economy.

A second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product growth is due Wednesday. The same day will bring the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures, as consumer prices keep rising faster than the 2% annual pace targeted by the central bank.

"The main message from the report is likely to be that pressure on goods prices is growing," economists at the Investment Institute by UniCredit said in a note. "Overall, October PCE data are likely to keep the Fed firmly on a hiking trajectory."

Durable goods orders, initial jobless claims and new home sales data are also due Wednesday along with the Summary of Commentary on Current Economic Conditions by Federal Reserve District, known as the Beige Book.

Markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving Holiday and will close early on Friday.

U.K.

The U.K. will have a relatively light data release calendar. The November flash estimate purchasing managers' index survey on Monday is the main event.

The U.K. composite PMI, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, rose to 52.9 in October, up from 52.0 in September and the highest reading since February.

"For the November report we imagine that the PMIs ticked higher again," Investec economists said in a note.

Activity might have received a boost from the absence of significant tax increases in the U.K. budget in October as some had feared, they said. U.S. President Trump refraining from renewed large-scale attacks on Iran following the midterm elections might have also helped, not least by helping to lower crude prices, they said. Investec forecasts the composite PMI will rise to 53.1 in November.

Elsewhere, the CBI distributive trades survey is due on Wednesday.

The U.K., meanwhile, plans to sell September 2049 index-linked gilt through syndicated sale, subject to demand and market conditions.

Eurozone

German, French and wider eurozone flash purchasing managers' surveys for November are due on Monday. The eurozone composite purchasing managers index, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, fell to a four-month low of 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September but remained above the 50 level that separates an expansion from a contraction.

"We expect to see some mild weakness in the euro-area PMIs, reflecting the challenging environment for energy markets and tighter financial conditions in Europe," RBC Capital Markets strategists said in a note.

On Tuesday, the German ifo business confidence survey for November will be released. That will be followed by the final third-quarter German gross domestic product report on Wednesday and GfK German consumer confidence survey for December on Thursday.

French and Spanish inflation data for November will be published Friday along with November German labor market data and the European Commission's business confidence survey.

Japan

Bank of Japan policy board member Naoki Tamura will meet with local leaders in the Yamanashi prefecture on Thursday. Investors will watch his remarks for clues on when the central bank might raise rates again.

Tokyo's November consumer-price data are due Friday. The figures are an early indicator of nationwide inflation, and a pickup could strengthen expectations for a rate increase.

BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda recently stressed the importance of keeping underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target. He said inflation excluding fresh food is likely to rise well above 2% as companies pass on higher labor costs, oil prices remain high and the yen stays weak.

The Ministry of Finance will auction about 300 billion yen of 40-year government bonds on Wednesday, reopening an issue first sold in May. The sale could draw demand from insurers and pension funds seeking long-dated debt.

The BOJ is scheduled to buy government bonds in three maturity ranges on Thursday, including those with more than three and up to five years remaining and those with more than 10 and up to 25 years remaining.

Japanese markets will be closed Monday for a national holiday.

China

A thin data slate awaits in China. The sole release of note drops Friday, which will show how China's industrial firms fared in October.

Economists will look at the figures to see if industrial profit growth held up last month after surging in September. Spending tied to artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure has been a key driver of profits over the year, though that hasn't benefited all sectors evenly.

Focus will also be on any potential announcements from Beijing after Xi Jinping's meetings with Trump didn't yield much in the way of progress on key trade and geopolitical issues. Markets will be watching ministry statements closely after Chinese officials warned of potential countermeasures to U.S. moves to tighten chip-export restrictions.

Australia / New Zealand

Australia's October inflation report on Wednesday will help shape expectations for the Reserve Bank of Australia's December rate decision. In September, annual headline inflation rose to 4.3% and trimmed-mean inflation climbed to 3.6%.

Third-quarter capital spending data due Thursday will show how much businesses invested and whether they revised their spending plans. The RBA will publish its bulletin the same day.

In New Zealand, third-quarter retail sales data due Monday will show how household spending is holding up ahead of the central bank's Dec. 9 rate decision.

South Korea

Bank of Korea is expected to raise its benchmark rate by a quarter-percentage-point to 3.25% on Thursday after leaving it unchanged in October.

Some analysts also expect the bank to raise its growth and inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027 as demand for chips used in artificial intelligence boosts exports and price pressures persist.

The central bank signaled it would raise its growth forecasts after third-quarter gross domestic product grew faster than expected. It expects inflation to stay above its 2% target through 2027.

The International Monetary Fund, the Korea Development Institute and Citi Research raised their growth forecasts for South Korea earlier this month, citing strength in the semiconductor industry.

Singapore

Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 1.9% in October from a year earlier, down from 2.2% in September, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core inflation, which excludes private road transport and accommodation costs, likely slowed to 1.6% from 2.0%, the poll showed. The data are due Monday.

Lower fourth-quarter electricity tariffs and a high year-earlier comparison likely helped ease inflation, said UOB economist Jester Koh.

Final third-quarter gross domestic product figures are due Tuesday. An advance estimate showed the economy grew 5.4% from a year earlier. DBS economists expect that figure to be revised up to 5.6%, mainly because manufacturing grew faster than initially reported.

DBS expects the government to forecast growth of 2.5% to 4.5% for 2027.

Any references to days are in local times.

data.title: IM Cannabis Corp. Appoints New CEO to Lead Technology-Driven Business Expansion
data.description:
Company also announces board changes, aligns with the Company's previously stated objective of evaluating and building technology-driven businesses beyond its core medical cannabis operations

VANCOUVER, BC and GLIL YAM, Israel, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IM Cannabis Corp. (the "Company") () announced changes to its management and board of directors (the "Board"), including the appointment of Ronen Zalayet as Chief Executive Officer and Ohad Melnik as an independent director.

Management Changes

Effective November 19, 2026, the Board appointed Ronen Zalayet as Chief Executive Officer of the Company, succeeding Oren Shuster, who resigned from that role.

Mr. Zalayet has more than 25 years of experience in financial leadership positions in private and public companies. He has served as Chief Financial Officer of Nexera Technologies Ltd. (formerly Jeffs' Brands Ltd.), a company listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq"), since October 2022. From July 2021 to December 2023, he served as Chief Executive Officer and a director of Shemen Oil and Gas Resources Ltd., a company listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. From July 2025 to June 2026, he served as Chief Financial Officer of Fort Technology Inc., a Canadian company listed on Nasdaq (formerly Impact Acquisition Corp.). From November 2019 to June 2021, Mr. Zalayet served as Chief Financial Officer of Colugo Systems Ltd., and from 2016 to 2020, he served as a consultant, a director and head of the Israeli office of Access Capital Markets Limited. Mr. Zalayet holds a B.A. in Economics and Accounting and an M.B.A. from Tel Aviv University and is a certified public accountant in Israel.

The Board thanks Mr. Shuster for his leadership of the Company since its founding and for his many contributions and welcomes Mr. Zalayet as Chief Executive Officer.

In addition, effective November 19, 2026, Shakked Shuster was appointed as Chief Executive Officer of Focus Medical Herbs Ltd., the Company's Israeli subsidiary through which it operates its medical cannabis business in Israel, succeeding Oren Shuster following his resignation from that role.

Mr. Shakked Shuster has more than six years of experience in Israel's medical cannabis industry through his work at the Company, spanning product, international sourcing, brand partnerships and marketing. He joined the Company in July 2020 as Product Marketing Lead before taking on the role of Product Manager from 2021 to 2022. In that role, he set the Company's product and quality standards and spent an extended period working with the team at its southern cultivation facility. Beginning in mid-2021, he led the development of the Company's import program, working with Canadian craft producers to establish supply from Canada to Israel. As Head of Product & Marketing from May 2022 to September 2023, he oversaw the product portfolio and the full marketing team. His work focused on expanding the product offering and strengthening international partnerships, including negotiating brand-licensing agreements and launching and developing the brands in the Israeli market. In September 2023, he stepped back from full-time management and continued working with the Company as an independent consultant, supporting business development with Canadian suppliers and exploring opportunities to bring new brands and products into Israel. Since May 2026, he has worked full time in the Company's Israeli operations.

Before joining the Company, Mr. Shakked Shuster served as a product designer in Unit 81, the technology unit of the Special Operations Division of the Israel Defense Forces' Intelligence Directorate, from 2016 to 2019.

Board Changes

Effective November 19, 2026, Oren Shuster resigned as a director of the Company and will continue to serve as a director of the Company's Israeli subsidiaries.

Effective November 19, 2026, Ohad Melnik was appointed to the Board to fill the vacancy created by the resignation of Einat Zakariya in September 2026. Mr. Melnik's appointment is subject to the approval of the Israel Medical Cannabis Agency (IMCA). The Board has determined that Mr. Melnik is an independent director under the Nasdaq listing rules.

Mr. Melnik served as a director of Formula Systems (1985) Ltd. from January 2019 to May 2024. He currently serves as an independent consultant on international online payments to the iFOREX Group and as a director of iFOR Fintech Ltd. an Israeli subsidiary of the iFOREX Group, and previously served as a director of the payment methods department and the finance compliance department of iFOREX International Group. He previously served as a director of Peninsula Group Ltd. from 2008 to 2015 and of Jerusalem Technology Investments Ltd. from 2012 to 2015. Mr. Melnik holds a B.A. in Business Administration and an M.B.A. (cum laude) from the College of Management, and is a graduate of the Executive M.S. in Finance program at Baruch College, City University of New York.

About IM Cannabis Corp.

IM Cannabis Corp. () is an international company operating a medical cannabis platform serving patients in Israel.

The Company's ecosystem operates in Israel through its subsidiaries, which import and distribute cannabis to medical patients, leveraging years of proprietary data and patient insights. The Company also operates medical cannabis retail pharmacies and online platforms in Israel that enable the safe delivery and quality control of IMCC's products throughout the value chain.
